The loop body executes only while `c < k` with `c` starting at 1, so `k ≤ 3` bounds it to at most two iterations, where `x` reaches `z² + z + 1` and `y` reaches `z²`. For any 32-bit `z` these stay below 2⁶³ in magnitude (worst case ≈ 4.6×10¹⁸), so no signed overflow, division, or shift UB occurs. Keeping `z` at its full declared range and capping `k` at 3 preserves roughly half the declared domain, far more than shrinking `z` for large `k` would.
